If TruuBlue felt interesting before, now may be the right time to take another look.

Download TruuBlue and meet people who want something real, with compatibility that goes deeper than a photo.

texto:
“I spent ten years studying couples separated by distance,” she said. “And the one thing that actually predicted survival was not love, or trust, or even how often the two of them talked.”

“The mistake is believing distance itself is the problem, when what actually kills these relationships is the absence of an end date that both people genuinely believe in.”

She explained that the couples who made it were not the ones with better communication or more passion. They were the ones who could name the month it ended. A date on a calendar turns distance into a project with a finish line. Without one, the same relationship becomes an open-ended wait, and the research was brutally clear about what happens next. Hope with no deadline slowly converts into resentment, and one person eventually starts building a life that has no room in it for the other, usually without ever consciously deciding to do it.

She also found that couples with a plan reported higher satisfaction than many couples living in the same city, which stopped surprising her once she understood why. Scarcity makes people intentional in a way that convenience never does.

After ten years of this research, she shares the four things the data showed.

Rule 1: Set a real end date, because distance with a finish line is a plan, while distance without one is simply waiting dressed up as love. A plan has a month attached to it.

Rule 2: Make sure you both believe the plan, because a date only one person actually intends to keep is not a plan at all, it is a story.

Rule 3: Notice if you are building a life without them, because the future you are carefully constructing reveals what you have already decided underneath all of it.

Rule 4: Treat the vagueness as the warning, because someone avoiding the date is avoiding the commitment sitting directly underneath it.

“Distance never once ended these relationships,” she said. “What ended them was two people waiting for something neither one had actually scheduled.”
